27/27 pass. Here's a summary of each decision:

**`BracketConfig`** — `final` class (not a record, because arrays have reference equality which would break record-generated `equals`/`hashCode`). The constructor clones both input arrays so callers can't mutate the config after construction. Fields are package-private (`final char[] closers/openers`) so `BracketMatcher` can access them without a method call per lookup. `BracketConfig.from(Map)` is the conversion boundary — boxing only happens once here when extracting map entries, not on every character comparison.

**`BracketMatcher`** — the record component changes from `Map<Character, Character>` to `BracketConfig`. All three methods now do primitive `char` comparisons in linear scans over the arrays. No `Character` objects are created during validation; every comparison is `char == char`. The `import java.util.Map` disappears entirely from this file.

**`BalancedParentheses`** — `DEFAULT_PAIRS` becomes `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (a `BracketConfig` literal) so the default path never touches a `Map` at runtime. A private `validate(String, BracketConfig)` overload holds the actual logic; the public `validate(String, Map)` converts once at the boundary and delegates. The public API signatures are unchanged.
